en: Mount Apo in Davao is the highest peak in the Philippines at 2,954 meters, not Mount Pulag.
Taal Volcano in Batangas is the most active volcano in the Philippines, not Mayon Volcano.
The Cagayan River in Northern Luzon is the longest river in the Philippines at 505 kilometers, not the Pasig River.
Lake Taal in Batangas is the deepest lake in the Philippines at 200 meters, whereas Laguna de Bay is merely the largest.
The West Philippine Sea lies on the western side of the archipelago, while the Philippine Sea is located to the east.
The critically endangered Philippine Eagle primarily inhabits the forests of Mindanao, not the islands of Luzon or the Visayas.
The famous Puerto Princesa Subterranean River is located in the province of Palawan, not in Cebu or Boracay.
The Cordillera Administrative Region is a geographical region composed of six provinces, not a single province itself.
Taal Volcano in Batangas holds the record as the smallest active volcano in the world, not the largest.
Mount Pinatubo is located on the island of Luzon across three provinces, not in the southern island of Mindanao.
The Galathea Depth in the Philippine Trench is the deepest point in the country at 10,540 meters, not the Manila Trench.
Luzon is the largest island in the Philippines, not Mindanao, covering over 109,000 square kilometers of land area.
